## Mitigation Checklist

When designing systems and processes, apply the following core security mitigations:

1. **Principle of Least Privilege** — Grant write scope only to the paths a process genuinely needs. Processes, scripts, and agents should operate under the minimum set of permissions required to complete their task; any broader capability expands the blast radius of a compromise.

2. **Input Validation at Trust Boundaries** — Treat all external content as untrusted data, never as instructions. Distinguish sharply between data (factual content to be processed or stored) and directives (procedural instructions to the system). Content arriving at a system boundary should never be parsed as commands to the system itself.

3. **Path Canonicalization** — Resolve and validate file paths before any write to block directory traversal. Symbolic links, relative paths (`../`), and other path-manipulation tricks can bypass intent-based access controls; canonicalize paths to their absolute, dereferenced form and validate against an allow list before performing I/O.

4. **Audit Logging** — Record every denied action with its reason for later review. When a security check rejects an operation, log it: what was attempted, who or what attempted it, when, and why it was rejected. This record is essential for forensics, compliance, and detection of attack patterns.
